question.knowledge_point: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Do Not Coincide
question.problem:
Find the limit at $x=3$ for the function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{3x-1}\, & \text{ for }\,x<3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(x\pi )\, & \text{ for }\,x\ge 3.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<3,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{3x-1}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}\sqrt[3]{3x-1} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{3\cdot 3-1} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{8} \\  & =2\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>3,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x\pi ).$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x\pi ) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\pi ) \\  & =-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the two limits are different, we can conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to 3}f(x)=\text{DNE}
$$

judgment.reasoning: All three earlier answers are confirmed by independent mathematics and their respective captured worked solutions. For q-36720, the left limit is 6(1/2)+1=4 and the right limit is -4 log_2(1/2)=4, so the two-sided limit is 4. For q-36724, the left limit is the cube root of 8, which is 2, while the right limit is cos(3π)=-1; unequal one-sided limits mean the two-sided limit does not exist. For q-37488, approaching zero from the left uses tan(x), which tends to 0. The choice's LaTeX spacing command does not change its equivalence to the source answer. No mathematical source errors or disagreements appear in these three solutions; no grades were supplied.
